$comment: HubSpot's app webhooks: a BATCH of CRM events pushed to the app's target URL, signed with signature v3. Read from developers.hubspot.com 'Validating requests' (2026-11-01), whose worked example reproduces from its inputs and is pinned in fancy-connector-core's signed-delivery corpus.
title: HubSpot CRM event
description: Start when HubSpot reports deals, contacts or companies created, changed, deleted, merged, restored or re-associated.
setup: In the HubSpot app's webhook settings, set the target URL to the route your host mounts for this trigger and subscribe to the deal, contact and company events you want. Deliveries are signed with the app's client secret, already on the connection as `clientSecret`. ONE URL serves every portal that installed the app, so route each event by its portalId, and only after the signature has verified: map portalId to the connection created when that portal installed, and drop an unmapped portalId with a 2xx and a log line, creating nothing. HubSpot retries a failed delivery, and eventId is not guaranteed to be unique, so never dedupe on eventId alone: a retry is the same event resent, differing only in attemptNumber, so compare every other field.

verification.$timestampComment: MILLISECONDS. HubSpot refuses nothing for you: a request older than 5 minutes must be rejected, and comparing the raw millisecond value with a window in seconds would reject every delivery ever made.
verification.$uriComment: The URL the request was sent to, with ONLY its query percent-decoded for twelve escapes, never the leading ?, any #fragment dropped. The host passes the request line exactly as it arrived; the core normalises.

$routeComment: MOIC's condition (2026-11-01): the payload's portalId is the only routing key an app-wide webhook has, and it is trustworthy only AFTER the signature verifies and only when it maps to a connection minted at install.

outputShape.description: HubSpot's id for this event. HubSpot says it is not guaranteed to be unique, so two different events can share one: never treat a repeated eventId alone as a duplicate.
Which of the app's subscriptions fired.
The portal (HubSpot account) the event happened in. The ONLY routing key, and only after verification.
The app the subscription belongs to.
When it happened, in epoch MILLISECONDS.
What happened: deal.creation, contact.propertyChange, company.deletion, … (object.* names on HubSpot's newer developer platform).
0 on the first delivery, counting up on retries. A retry differs from the original ONLY here.
The record the event is about. Pass it to deal_get / contact_get / company_get as a string.
CREATED, DELETED, MERGED, RESTORED, … where the event type carries one.
What made the change: CRM_UI, API, IMPORT, …
For a property change: which property. Absent otherwise.
For a property change: its new value, as a string. Absent otherwise.
